title: Choose the visual world for the Daiko webui
question: The roll assigned The Inspector. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Inspector
options.lineage: DOS-era file managers & database browsers (Norton Commander, Turbo Vision), modernized
options.thesis: Your agents' shared brain is one SQLite file on your machine — the UI is that file made visible, dressed as the file-manager grammar developers already trust.
options.viewport: A full-bleed cobalt field. Top strip: DAIKO left, the literal db path ~/.daiko/daiko.db center, store size right. Below, panels framed by fine rules with titles set into the border — STORE counts as a ruled table row, RECENT ACTIVITY as true rows with hashes; hovering runs a cyan inverse-video selection bar across them. A fixed bottom key-bar names real commands.
options.risk: Retro pastiche can tire or hurt legibility if played as costume; the cobalt field commits the whole surface — this is a loud calm, not a neutral one. Mitigated by modern type scale, generous spacing, and restrained ornament.

options.label: Design Annual Plate Section
options.lineage: print annuals: registration crosshairs, hairlines, letterpress stamp
options.thesis: Artifacts as printed plates on near-white stock; every save is a new edition in the credits row.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and carries the calm — but a print-annual identifies designers, not terminal-native developers; loses on audience identification.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.lineage: printer's zone-system record cards under the enlarger
options.thesis: Versions as exposure records: translucent sheets, hatch densities, stop-deltas for diffs.
options.case: The annotation grammar is seductive for version history, but hatches and stop-deltas map obliquely to sync/pin — loses on product clarity.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: stage lighting: cue stacks on an infinite horizon
options.thesis: Version history as a lighting cue stack — scrub from first light (v1) to day (current).
options.case: The scrubbable cue timeline is a genuinely good version-history idea, but the atmospheric world fuses poorly with tables of artifacts — loses both axes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The polished dark developer dashboard — neutral near-black, one blue accent, rounded cards — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, stat cards, tables; what the current UI reaches for, finished impeccably.
